title: FEMA's ‘Shadow Administrator’ Was Paid by a DOGE Member's Startup for Months
gist: Court filings in an AFGE lawsuit show Kara Voorhies, the outside contractor described as FEMA's 'shadow administrator,' was paid $325/hour through a three-layer subcontract chain running from prime contractor IMGE to AnchorCode Technologies — a company owned by DOGE operative Kyle Schutt — to her own one-person LLC. The structure kept both intermediate firms out of the federal System for Award Management, so no public database showed who was actually reviewing FEMA contracts and terminating grants.

insights.claim: Kara Voorhies, the outside contractor described as FEMA's 'shadow administrator,' was paid from October 1, 2025 to mid-March 2026 through a three-tier chain: her one-person firm LV Consulting subcontracted to AnchorCode Technologies, owned by DOGE operative Kyle Schutt, which subcontracted to prime contractor IMGE, the only entity holding a direct DHS contract.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Prime-contractor disclosure is the only visible layer in federal procurement data, so vendor-exposure screens built on SAM filings systematically miss who is actually performing agency work.
insights.quote: In October, this company began serving as a subcontractor to AnchorCode Technologies, which was owned by Schutt and was itself already serving as a subcontractor to another company, IMGE.
insights.locator: In her deposition, Voorhies said that in September 2025

insights.claim: Second- and third-tier federal subcontractors do not appear in the System for Award Management, the public database of companies contracting with the US government, meaning any procurement-transparency analysis built on SAM data is structurally blind to the actual performers of the work.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Treat SAM-derived government-revenue estimates for any vendor as a floor, not a census; subcontract flow is invisible to the standard data source.
insights.quote: As subcontractors, AnchorCode and LV Consulting did not have direct contracts with DHS and do not appear in the System for Award Management, the system that shows which companies contract with the government.

insights.claim: Voorhies was paid $325 an hour for her contractor work with AnchorCode and testified she did not have to go through any public bidding process to win the engagement.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: A no-bid pass-through rate is the kind of specific, documentable number that turns an 'optics' story into an enforcement or clawback story.
insights.locator: For her work as a contractor with AnchorCode

insights.claim: Both Schutt and Voorhies retained the title of senior adviser at DHS after converting from government personnel to contractors, and Voorhies testified she never informed DHS colleagues that her employment status had changed.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: When titles do not track employment status, internal agency controls that key off 'is this person a federal employee' silently fail — a template for how similar arrangements go undetected elsewhere.
insights.locator: Both Schutt and Voorhies retained their titles

insights.claim: Special government employees face fewer transparency and disclosure requirements than federal employees but are capped at 130 working days per year, and when Voorhies hit that cap in fall 2025 the workaround she and Schutt devised was to re-enter the same agency as a subcontractor.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: The 130-day cap creates a predictable conversion event: watch for SGE-to-subcontractor flips as the moment influence becomes commercially monetized.
insights.quote: SGEs are subject to fewer transparency and disclosure requirements than federal employees but are limited to working in government for 130 days per year.
insights.locator: Voorhies, who had no previous government experience

insights.claim: A contractor with no prior government experience was reviewing the memos accompanying FEMA contracts and grant requests above $100,000 and was involved in reviewing and terminating FEMA grants, work that federal law reserves as 'inherently governmental functions.'
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Grant and contract terminations executed by an improperly situated reviewer are legally reversible, creating contingent restoration liability for terminated FEMA awards.
insights.quote: “Federal law prohibits government contractors from performing work that is characterized as ‘inherently governmental functions,’”

insights.claim: An ethics lawyer formerly with the Office of Government Ethics assesses that Voorhies was senior enough at FEMA to have been subject to a two-year post-employment communications ban, and that absent a waiver — none was findable on the Federal Register — the arrangement violated 18 USC 207 of the criminal code.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Criminal-statute framing, not just 'appearance' framing, is what escalates a procurement story into personal exposure for the individuals and disqualification risk for the firms.
insights.quote: Based on her understanding of Voorhies’ situation, Dylus-Yukins alleges, "this is illegal under 18 USD 207 of the criminal code.”
insights.locator: Margaret Dylus-Yukins, senior legal counsel for ethics

themes.theme: DOGE alumni as a contracting class

insights.claim: Kyle Schutt rotated across the General Services Administration, CISA, HHS, and DHS while earning $195,000 as a GSA employee, and GSA's core function is acquisition and procurement — making it highly likely he was exposed to procurement-sensitive data before his own company began subcontracting to DHS.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Cross-agency placement plus a procurement-heavy host agency is the specific fact pattern that converts an access question into an information-advantage question in bid protests.
insights.quote: “An important ethics question would also be whether he became privy to procurement-sensitive data while he was a federal employee at DHS, which is highly likely if he was at GSA, because the main thing they do is acquisition and procurement,”
insights.locator: Schutt’s employment at GSA, the employee says

insights.claim: Schutt's login credentials were compromised by malware, revealed in May 2025 after reporting that he had been granted access to FEMA's payment software — an operational security failure at the exact node controlling federal disaster disbursements.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Credential compromise on a payment system is the concrete downside of fast-tracked access grants — a recurring tail risk in every 'efficiency' staffing push.
insights.locator: In May 2025 it was revealed that Schutt’s login credentials

insights.claim: Schutt is not an isolated case: former DOGE member Ethan Shaotran was reported to be launching a defense tech startup positioned to receive government contracts, indicating a repeatable pattern of DOGE tenure converting into contract access.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: A cohort of newly formed, politically connected govtech and defense-tech vendors is forming; expect them in cap tables and competitive bids before they appear in procurement databases.
insights.locator: Schutt is not the only DOGE member

themes.theme: Litigation and political-cycle risk for the vendors

insights.claim: A government-procurement law academic argues that rival contractors could sue IMGE on the theory that subcontracting to Schutt and Voorhies gave the company an unfair advantage, opening a private-litigation channel independent of any government enforcement action.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Bid-protest and unfair-advantage suits can freeze a vendor's pipeline long before any criminal or IG process concludes — the faster-moving risk for IMGE's parent GP3 Partners.
insights.locator: Jessica Tillipman, associate dean for government procurement law studies

insights.claim: Voorhies' AnchorCode contract was terminated in mid-March 2026, one week after Trump announced he would replace Kristi Noem as Homeland Security secretary, showing these arrangements were tied to individual political patrons rather than to institutional need.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Patron-linked contract revenue reprices instantly on a cabinet reshuffle — a durability discount that applies to any vendor whose access traces to one appointee.
insights.locator: It is not clear from Voorhies’ deposition when AnchorCode’s contract

insights.claim: IMGE, the prime contractor, is a political marketing agency selling 'audience intelligence, advanced advertising, AI-powered analytics, influencer marketing' whose prior clients include Rand Paul's campaign and Mike Pence's Advancing American Freedom, an unusual profile for holding a direct DHS contract.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Mismatch between a prime's commercial specialty and the contract's subject matter is a cheap screening signal for pass-through arrangements.
insights.locator: IMGE describes itself as a “full-service” marketing agency

insights.claim: The Trump administration has repeatedly signaled it wants to eliminate FEMA, and 25 Democratic-led states filed suit alleging disaster aid was cut to them in retaliation to coerce use of USCIS's SAVE database for voter-roll checks against DHS immigration records.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Disaster-aid flows are being used as policy leverage, which makes state-level fiscal exposure to federal reimbursement a live credit variable rather than a routine assumption.
